translations.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
He was in the beginning with God.
All things were made through him, and without him not one thing was made of all that was made.
With him was life, and that life was the light of men.
And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overtake it.
There was a man sent by God, and his name was John.
He came as a witness, to bear witness to the light, so that all might believe through him.
He was not the light himself, but came to bear witness to the light.
There was the true light, which gives light to every person coming into the world.
He was in the world, and the world was made through him, and the world did not know him.
He came to his own, and his own did not receive him.
But to as many as received him he gave the power to become children of God, to those who believe in his name,
who were born not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of a man, but of God.
And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory, glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth.
John bore witness to him; he cried out and said: "This is the one of whom I said: He who comes after me has come to be before me, for he is prior to me."
And from his fullness we have all received, and grace in place of grace.
For the Law was given through Moses, but grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
No one has ever seen God; the only-begotten Son, who was in the bosom of the Father, he has made him known.
And this is the testimony of John, when the Jews sent priests and Levites to him from Jerusalem to ask him, "Who are you?"
And he confessed and did not deny; he confessed, "I am not the Christ."
And they asked him, "Then who are you? Are you Elijah?" And he said, "I am not." "Are you the Prophet?" And he answered, "No."
And they said to him, "Tell us who you are, so that we may bring an answer to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?"
And he said, "I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness: Make ready the ways of the Lord, as the prophet Isaiah said."
And those who had been sent were from among the Pharisees.
They questioned him and said to him, "Why then do you baptize, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?"
John answered and said to them: I baptize with water, but among you stands one whom you do not know,
who is to come after me, who was before me, whose sandal straps I am not worthy to untie.
This took place in Bethabara, beyond the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him, and said: Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world.
This is he of whom I said: After me comes a man who was before me, for he is greater than I.
And I did not know him; but so that he might be revealed to Israel, for this reason I came baptizing with water.
And John bore witness and said: I saw the Spirit of God coming down from heaven like a dove, and it remained upon him.

And I did not know him; but the one who sent me to baptize with water said to me: The one on whom you see the Spirit coming down and remaining upon him, he is the one who will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.
And I have seen and borne witness that this is the Son of God.
The next day John was again standing there with two of his disciples.
And he looked at Jesus as he walked by, and said: Behold, the Lamb of God!
And the two disciples heard him say this, and they followed Jesus.
Jesus turned and saw them following him, and said to them: What are you seeking? And they said to him: Rabbi (which is translated Teacher), where are you staying?
He said to them: Come and see! And they went and saw where he was staying, and they remained with him that day. It was about the tenth hour.
Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two who had heard John and followed him.
He first found his own brother Simon and said to him: We have found the Messiah, which is translated Christ.
He brought him to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said: You are Simon, son of Jonah; you shall be called Cephas, which is translated Rock.
The next day Jesus wished to go out to Galilee, and he found Philip, and Jesus said to him: Follow me!
Now Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.
Philip found Nathanael and said to him: The one of whom Moses wrote in the Law, and the prophets, we have found: Jesus, son of Joseph, from Nazareth.
And Nathanael said to him: Can anything good come from Nazareth? Philip said to him: Come and see!
When Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him, he said of him: Behold, truly an Israelite, in whom there is no deceit.
Nathanael said to him: How do you know me? Jesus answered and said to him: Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you.
Nathanael answered him and said: Rabbi, you are the Son of God, you are the King of Israel!
Jesus answered and said to him: Because I told you that I saw you under the fig tree, you believe? You will see greater things than these.
And he said to them: "Truly, truly I say to you: from now on you will see the heavens opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man."
And on the third day there was a wedding at Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there.
Jesus and his disciples were invited to that wedding.
And when the wine ran short, his mother said to Jesus: "They have no wine."
Jesus said to her: "What is there between me and you, woman? My hour has not yet come."
His mother said to the servants: "Whatever he tells you, do it!"
Six stone water jars were standing there, for the purification rites of the Jews, each of which held two or three measures.
And Jesus said to them: "Fill those jars with water!" And they filled them to the brim.
And he said to them: "Now draw some out and take it to the master of the feast!" And they took it.

And when the master of the feast tasted the water that had become wine, and did not know where it came from (though the servants who had filled them with water knew), the master of the feast called the bridegroom
and said to him: "Everyone serves the good wine first, and when people have become drunk, then the worse. But you have kept the good wine until now."
Jesus did this, the first of his signs, at Cana of Galilee, and revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.
After this Jesus went down to Capernaum, he and his mother and his brothers and his disciples with him, and he stayed there not many days.
And the Passover of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
And in the temple he found sellers of oxen and sheep and doves, and money-changers sitting there.
And he made a whip of cord and drove them all out of the temple, the oxen and the sheep; and he poured out the coins of the money-changers and overturned their tables.
And to the dove-sellers he said: "Take these things away from here, and do not make my Father's house a house of trade."
And his disciples remembered that it is written: "Zeal for your house has consumed me."
The Jews answered and said to him: "What sign do you show us, since you do these things?"
Jesus answered and said: "Destroy this temple, and on the third day I will raise it up."
The Jews said to him: "This temple was built in forty-six years, and will you raise it up in three days?"
But he was speaking of the temple of his body.
And when he rose from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed the scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken to them.
And when he was in Jerusalem at the feast of Passover, many believed in his name, because they saw the signs that he was doing.
But Jesus himself did not entrust himself to them, because he knew them all.
And because he had no need that anyone should testify about man, for he himself knew what was in man.
There was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews.
He came to Jesus by night and said to him: "Rabbi, we know that you have come from God as a teacher, for no one can do these signs that you do unless God is with him."
Jesus answered and said to him: "Amen, amen, I say to you: unless someone is born a second time, he cannot see the kingdom of heaven."
Nicodemus said to him: "How can an old man be born? Is it possible for him to enter his mother's womb a second time and be born?"
Jesus answered and said to him: "Amen, amen, I say to you: unless someone is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.
What is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit.
Do not be amazed that I said this to you: you must be born a second time.
The Spirit blows wherever it wills, and you hear its voice, but you do not know where it comes from or where it goes. So it is with everyone who is born of the Spirit."
Nicodemus answered and said to him: "How can this be?"
Jesus answered and said to him: "You are the teacher of Israel, and you do not know this?
Amen, amen, I say to you: we speak of what we know, and we testify to what we have seen, and you do not accept our testimony.
If I have told you earthly things and you do not believe, how then will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?
And no one has gone up into heaven except the one who came down from heaven, the Son of Man, who is in heaven.
And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up,
so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but may have eternal life.
For God so loved this world that he gave his only-begotten Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but may have eternal life.
For God did not send his Son into the world to condemn the world, but so that the world might be saved through him.
Whoever believes in him is not condemned; but whoever does not believe is already condemned, because he has not believed in the name of the only-begotten Son of God.
And this is the judgment: that the light has come into the world, and people loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.
For everyone who does evil hates the light and does not come to the light, so that his deeds may not be exposed.
But whoever does the truth comes to the light, so that his deeds may be made plain, because they have been done through God."
After this Jesus and his disciples came into the land of Judea, and he stayed there with them and baptized.
John too was baptizing at Aenon, near Salim, because there was much water there, and people were coming and being baptized by him.
For John had not yet been thrown into prison.
And there arose a dispute between John's disciples and the Jews about purification.
And they came to John and said to him: "Rabbi, the one who was with you beyond the Jordan, the one you bore witness to: look, he is baptizing, and everyone is going to him."
John answered and said to them: "A man cannot receive anything at all by himself unless it has been given to him from heaven.
You yourselves are my witnesses that I said, 'I am not the Christ, but I have been sent ahead of him.'
The one who has the bride is the bridegroom. But the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom's voice. So this joy of mine is fulfilled.
He must increase, but I must decrease.
The one who comes from above is above all. And the one who is from the earth is of the earth and speaks of earthly things, but the one who comes from heaven is above all.
And he bears witness to what he has seen and heard, yet no one accepts his testimony.
Whoever has accepted his testimony has set his seal to this: that God is true.
And the one whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for God does not give the Spirit by measure.
The Father loves the Son and has given everything into his hands.
Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life, but whoever disobeys the Son will not see life; instead, the wrath of God remains on him."
When the Lord learned that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus had more disciples and was baptizing more than John
(although Jesus himself did not baptize; his disciples did),
he left Judea and went away to Galilee.
But he had to pass through Samaria.
And he came to a city of the Samaritans called Sychar, near the plot of land that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
Jacob's spring was there, and Jesus, tired from the journey, sat down by the spring. It was about the sixth hour.
A woman came from Samaria to draw water. Jesus said to her: "Give me water to drink!"
(For his disciples had gone away into the city to buy food.)
The Samaritan woman said to him: "How is it that you, a Jew, ask me for water, a Samaritan woman?" (For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.)
Jesus answered and said to her: "If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who is saying to you, 'Give me water to drink,' you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water."
The woman said to him: "Lord, you do not even have a bucket to draw with, and this well is deep. So where do you get living water?
Are you greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well? He himself drank from it, and so did his sons and his flocks."
Jesus answered and said to her: "Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again.
But whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again for ever; rather, the water that I will give him will become in him a spring of water flowing to eternal life.
The woman said to him: "Lord, give me this water, so that I will not thirst and will not come here any more to draw water."
Jesus said to her: "Go, call your husband, and come here!"
The woman answered and said to him: "I have no husband." Jesus said to her: "You said well, 'I have no husband,'
for you have had five husbands, and the one you have now is not your husband. What you have said is true."
The woman said to him: "Lord, I see that you are a prophet.
Our fathers worshipped on this mountain, and you say that Jerusalem is the place where one ought to worship."
Jesus said to her: "Woman, believe me, the hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.
You worship what you do not know; but we worship what we know, for salvation is from the Jews.
But the hour is coming, and is already here, when the true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father also seeks such as these to be his worshippers.
God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth."
The woman said to him: "I know that the Messiah is coming, who is called Christ. When he comes, he will tell us everything."
Jesus said to her: "I am he, who is speaking to you."
And just at this word his disciples came, and they were amazed that he was speaking with a woman. Yet no one said to him, "What are you seeking?" or, "Why are you speaking with her?"
Then the woman left her water jar and went away into the city and said to the people:
"Come and see a man who told me everything that I have done. Could he be the Christ?"
They went out of the city and were coming to him.
And while they were coming, at that very time the disciples were speaking to him and said: "Rabbi, eat!"
But he said to them: "I have food to eat that you do not know about."
The disciples said to one another: "Has someone brought him food?"
Jesus said to them: "My food is to do the will of the one who sent me and to accomplish his work.
Do you not say, 'There are four months more, and then comes the harvest'? Look, I tell you: lift up your eyes and see the fields, for they are already white for harvest.
And the reaper receives his wages and gathers fruit for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together with him.
For in this the saying is true, that one is the sower and another is the reaper.
I send you to reap that for which you did not labor. Others have labored, and you have entered into their labor."
And many of the Samaritans from that city believed in him because of what the woman said, for she testified: "He told me everything I have done."
And when the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay with them. And he stayed there two days.
And a much greater number believed because of his words.
And they said to the woman: "We no longer believe because of what you said, for we have heard him ourselves, and we know that this is truly the Saviour of the world, the Christ."
After those two days he went out from there and went away to Galilee.
For Jesus himself testified that a prophet has no honour in his own country.
When he came to Galilee, the Galileans welcomed him, for they had seen everything he had done in Jerusalem at the feast, because they too had come to the feast.
Jesus came again to Cana of Galilee, where he had turned the water into wine. And there was a certain man from the royal court whose son was sick in Capernaum.
This man heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee. He came to him and begged him to go with him and heal his son, who was close to death.
Jesus said to him: "Unless you see signs and wonders, you will not believe."
The royal official said to him: "Lord, come before my son dies."
Jesus said to him: "Go, your son lives!" And the man believed the word that Jesus had spoken to him, and he went away.
And while he was still on his way, his servants came to meet him. They told him: "Your son lives."
He asked them: "At what hour did he get better?" They said to him: "Yesterday, at the seventh hour, the fever left him."
The boy's father remembered that this was the very hour when Jesus had said to him: "Your son lives." And he believed, and so did his whole household.
This was the second sign that Jesus did when he came from Judea to Galilee.
After this there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
And in Jerusalem, at the Sheep Bath, there is a pool that is called Bethesda in Hebrew, and it had five porticoes.
In these lay a crowd of sick people: blind, lame and withered. They were waiting for the water to be stirred.
For year by year an angel would come down to the pool and stir the water. Whoever went down first after the water was stirred was healed of whatever disease he suffered from.
There was a certain man there who had spent thirty-eight years in sickness.
Jesus saw him lying there and knew that he had been sick for many years. Jesus said to him: "Do you want to be healed?"
The sick man answered him: "Lord, I have no one to put me into this pool when the water is stirred. While I am coming, someone else goes down before me and is healed."
Jesus said to him: "Get up, pick up your bed and walk!"
And at once the man was restored to health. He picked up his bed and went away. Now that day was the Sabbath.
The Jews were saying to him: "It is the Sabbath, and it is not lawful for you to take up your bed."
But he answered and said to them: "The one who healed me said to me: 'Take up your bed and walk!'"
So the Jews questioned him and said: "Who is the man who said to you, 'Take up your bed and walk'?"
But the man who had been healed did not know who it was, for Jesus had slipped away, because there was a crowd in that place.
After this Jesus found him in the temple and said to him: "See, you have been made well; sin no more, so that nothing worse may happen to you."
The man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had healed him.
And for this reason the Jews persecuted Jesus and wanted to kill him, because he was doing these things on the Sabbath.
But Jesus answered and said to them: "My Father is working until now, and I also am working."
For this reason the Jews sought all the more to kill Jesus, because not only was he breaking the Sabbath, but he was also calling God his own Father, making himself equal to God.

Jesus answered and said to them: "Amen, amen, I say to you: the Son of Man cannot do anything at all of himself, unless he sees the Father doing something; for whatever the Father does, the Son likewise does in the same way.
For the Father loves the Son and shows him everything that he himself does, and he will show him works greater than these, so that you will marvel.
For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom he wills.
Nor does the Father judge anyone, but he has given all judgment to the Son,
so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. For whoever does not honor the Son has not honored the Father who sent him.
Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever has heard my words and has believed the one who sent me has eternal life, and he will not come into judgment, but will pass from death to life.
Amen, amen, I say to you: the hour is coming, and is now here, when the dead will hear the words of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
For just as the Father has life in himself, so he has also granted the Son to have life in himself.
And he has given him authority to execute judgment as well, because he is the Son of Man.
Do not marvel at this, for the hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs will hear his voice.
And they will come out: those who have done good, to the resurrection of life, but those who have done evil, to the resurrection of judgment.
I can do nothing at all of myself; as I hear, I judge, and my judgment is just, because I do not seek my own will but the will of the Father who sent me.
If I bear witness about myself, my testimony is not true.
There is another who bears witness about me, and I know that the testimony he bears about me is true.
You sent to John, and he bore witness to the truth.
But I do not accept testimony from man; rather, I say these things so that you may be saved.
He was a lamp, lit and shining, and you were willing for a time to rejoice in his light.
But I have a testimony greater than John's, for the works which the Father gave me to accomplish, these very works which I do, testify about me, that the Father has sent me.
And the one who sent me, the Father, has himself testified about me. You have never heard his voice, nor have you seen his form.
And his word does not abide in you, for you do not believe the one whom God has sent.
Search the Scriptures, for you think that you have eternal life in them; and it is they that testify about me.
And you do not want to come to me, so that you may have life.
I do not receive glory from men.
But I know you, that you do not have the love of God within yourselves.
I have come in the name of my Father, and you do not receive me. If another comes in his own name, him you will receive.
How then can you believe, since you receive glory from one another and do not seek the glory of the only God?
Do not think that I will accuse you before my Father; there is one who accuses you, Moses, in whom you have set your hope.
If you had believed Moses, you would have believed me also, for he wrote about me.
If you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my words?
After this Jesus crossed over to the other side of the Sea of Galilee, that is, of Tiberias.
And a great crowd followed him, because they saw the signs which he was performing on the sick.
And Jesus went up onto the mountain and sat down there with his disciples.
And the Passover, the feast of the Jews, was near.
Jesus lifted up his eyes and saw that a great crowd was coming to him. He said to Philip, "Where shall we buy bread, so that these may eat?"
He said this to test him, for he himself knew what he was about to do.
Philip said to him, "Two hundred drachmas' worth of bread is not enough for them, for each one to receive even a little."
One of his disciples, Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, said to him,
"There is a boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what are these among so many?"
Jesus said to him, "Make these men sit down!" And there was much grass in that place, and the men sat down, about five thousand in number.
And Jesus took the loaves and gave thanks and gave them to the disciples, and the disciples gave them to the people who were seated; and likewise of the fish, as much as they wanted.
And when they were filled, he said to his disciples, "Gather up the leftover fragments, so that nothing may be lost."
So they gathered them up and filled twelve baskets with the fragments from the five barley loaves that were left over by those who had eaten.
When the people saw the sign that Jesus had done, they said, "This is truly the prophet who has come into the world."
But Jesus perceived that they were about to come and seize him to make him king, and he withdrew and went away to the mountain, alone by himself.
When evening came, his disciples went down to the sea.
They got into the boat and were crossing the sea to Capernaum. It had already grown dark, and Jesus had not yet come to them,
and the sea was stirred up by a great wind.
When they had gone about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they saw Jesus walking on the sea; and as he came near the boat, they were afraid.
But he said to them, "It is I; do not be afraid!"
They wanted to take him into the boat, and immediately the boat was at the land to which they were going.

On the next day the crowd that stood on the other side of the sea knew that there had been no other boat there except the one which Jesus' disciples had entered, and that Jesus had not gone into the boat with the disciples, but only his disciples had gone.
Then other boats came from Tiberias, near the place where they had eaten the bread which the Lord blessed and over which he gave thanks.
When the crowd saw that Jesus was not there, nor his disciples, they brought up those boats, came to Capernaum, and looked for Jesus.
And they found him on the other side of the sea and said to him, "Rabbi, when did you come here?"
Jesus answered and said to them, "Amen, amen, I say to you: you seek me not because you saw signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled.
Do not labor for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you; for on him the Father, God, has set his seal."
They said to him, "What shall we do, that we may perform the work of God?"
Jesus answered and said to them, "This is the work of God: that you believe in him whom he has sent."
And they said to him, "What sign do you perform, that we may see and believe you? What do you do?
Our fathers ate manna in the wilderness, as it is written: 'He gave them bread from heaven to eat.'"
Jesus said to him, "Amen, amen, I say to you: it was not Moses who gave you bread from heaven, but my Father gives you the true bread from heaven.
For the bread of God is that which came down from heaven and gave life to the world."
They said to him, "Lord, give us this bread always!"
Jesus said to them, "I am the bread of life; whoever comes to me will not hunger, and whoever believes in me will never thirst.
But I said to you that you have seen me and do not believe.
All that my Father has given me will come to me; and whoever comes to me I will not cast out.
For I came down from heaven not to do my own will, but the will of my Father who sent me.
And this is the will of my Father who sent me: that of all that he has given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up on the last day.
For this is the will of him who sent me: that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him should have eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.
The Jews murmured about him because he said, "I am the bread that came down from heaven," --
and they said, "Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then does he say, 'I came down from heaven'?"
Jesus answered and said to them, "Do not murmur among yourselves!
No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me brings him to me, and I will raise him up on the last day.
It is written in the prophets: 'They shall all be taught by God.' Everyone who hears from my Father and learns comes to me.
Not that anyone has seen the Father; but the one who is from God, he has seen the Father.
Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever believes in me has eternal life.
I am the bread of life.
Your fathers ate manna in the wilderness and died.
This is the bread that came down from heaven; if anyone eats of it, he will not die.

I am the living bread that came down from heaven. If anyone eats of this bread, he will not die but will live forever. And the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world."
The Jews argued among themselves and said, "How can this man give us his own flesh to eat?"
Jesus said to them, "Amen, amen, I say to you: unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in yourselves.
But whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.
For my flesh is true food, and my blood is true drink.
And whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood abides with me, and I with him.
As the living Father sent me, and I too live with the Father, so whoever eats of me will also live through me.
For this is the bread that came down from heaven. It is not like the manna your fathers ate and died. But whoever eats this bread will live forever."
He said this in the synagogue as he was teaching in Capernaum.
So many of his disciples heard this and said, "This saying is hard. Who can listen to it?"
Jesus knew in himself that his disciples were murmuring about this, and he said to them, "Does this make you stumble?
What if you see the Son of Man ascending to where he was before?
The spirit is what gives life, but the flesh is of no benefit. The words that I speak to you are spirit and life,
but there are some of you who do not believe. — For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were who did not believe, and who it was who would betray him.
And he said: This is why I told you that no one can come to me unless it has been granted to him by my Father.
Because of this many of his disciples turned back and no longer went about with him.
Jesus said to the Twelve: Do you also want to go away?
Simon Peter answered him and said: Lord, to whom shall we go? For you have the words of eternal life.
And we have believed and have come to know that you are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
Jesus answered and said to them: Did I not choose you, the Twelve? And one of you is a devil.
He was speaking of Judas son of Simon, the Iscariot, who was one of the Twelve, for he was going to betray him.
After this Jesus went about in Galilee and did not want to go to Judea, because the Jews were seeking to kill him.
Now the feast of the Jews, the feast of Tabernacles, was near.
His brothers said to him: Leave here and go to Judea, so that your disciples too may see the works that you are doing!
For no one does anything in secret while seeking to be known publicly. If you do these things, show yourself to the world!
For not even his brothers believed in him.
Jesus said to them: My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready.
The world cannot hate you, but it hates me, because I testify about it that its works are evil.
You go up to this feast. I am not going up to this feast, because my time has not yet been fulfilled.
He said this to them and stayed in Galilee.
And when his brothers had gone up to the feast, then Jesus himself also went up, not openly but as it were in secret.
The Jews were looking for him at the feast and saying: Where is he?
And there was much murmuring about him among the people. Some were saying: He is a good man; but others were saying: No, he is leading the people astray.
Yet no one spoke openly about him for fear of the Jews.
And when the feast was already half over, Jesus went up to the temple and began teaching.
The Jews were amazed and said: How does this man know the Scriptures without having been taught?
Jesus answered and said: This teaching of mine is not mine, but belongs to the one who sent me.
If anyone does his will, he will know this teaching, what it is: whether it is from God, or whether I speak of myself.
Whoever speaks of himself seeks his own glory; but whoever seeks the glory of the one who sent him is true, and there is no falsehood in him.
Did not Moses give you the law? Yet none of you keeps the law. Why do you seek to kill me?
The people answered and said to him: You have a demon. Who is seeking to kill you?
Jesus answered and said to them: I did one deed among you, and you all marvel.
For this reason Moses gave you circumcision (not that it is from Moses, but from the fathers), and a man is circumcised on the sabbath.
If a man receives circumcision on the sabbath so that the law of Moses may not be broken, do you blame me because I made a man entirely well on the sabbath?
Do not judge by appearances, but judge with righteous judgment.
Some of the people of Jerusalem were saying: Is this not the man whom they were seeking to kill?
Look, he is speaking openly, and they say nothing to him. Can it be that the rulers have truly come to know that this is truly the Christ?
But we know where this man is from. When the Christ comes, no one will know where he is from.
Jesus cried out in the temple as he was teaching, and said: You both know me and you know where I am from. And I have not come of myself, and he is true. The one who sent me, you do not know.
But I know him, for I am from him, and he sent me.
They sought to seize him, but no one laid hands on him, because his hour had not yet come.
And many of the people believed in him, and they were saying: When the Christ comes, will he do more signs than this man has done?
And the Pharisees heard the people murmuring about him. And the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to seize him,
and Jesus said: I am with you a little while longer, and then I go to the one who sent me.
You will seek me and will not find me, and where I am, you cannot come.
The Jews were saying to one another: Where does this man intend to go, that we will not find him? Does he intend to go to the dispersion among the Gentiles and teach the Gentiles there?
What is this saying of his: 'You will seek me and will not find me,' and 'Where I am, you cannot come'?
And on the last day, the great day of the feast, Jesus stood up and cried out, saying: If anyone is thirsty, let him come to me and drink.
And whoever believes in me, as the scripture has said, rivers of living water will flow from his belly.
He said this about the Spirit, which those who believed in him were to receive; for the Holy Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.
Many of the people heard this saying, and they were saying: This is truly the prophet.
Others were saying: This is the Christ. But others were saying: Is the Christ to come from Galilee, then?
Does the Scripture not say that the Christ will come from the seed of David and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?
And there was a division among the people because of him.
And some of them wanted to seize him, but no one laid hands on him.
The servants came to the chief priests and the Pharisees, and they said to them: "Why did you not bring him?"
The servants answered and said to them: "Never has any man spoken the way this man speaks."
The Pharisees answered and said to them: "Have you too perhaps been led astray?"
Has any of the rulers, or of the Pharisees, believed in him?
But this people, which does not know the Law, is accursed."
Nicodemus, who had come to him earlier and was one of them, said to them:
"Does our Law condemn a man unless it first hears from him and learns what he is doing?"
They answered and said to him: "Are you also from Galilee? Search and see, for no prophet has arisen from Galilee."
And each one went to his own house.
But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
And at dawn he came again to the Temple, and all the people were coming to him, and he sat down and was teaching them.
Then the scribes and the Pharisees brought to him a woman who had been caught openly, in public, in adultery, and they set her in the midst
and said to him, for they were testing him: "Teacher, this woman was caught openly in adultery.
And in our Law Moses commanded that such women be stoned. What then do you say?"
They said this to test him, so that they might have grounds to accuse him. But Jesus bent down to the ground and was writing on the ground with his finger, and said nothing to them.
And as they stood a long while and kept asking him, he straightened up and said to them: "Whoever of you is without sin, let him be the first to throw a stone at her."
And again he bent down and was writing on the ground.
When they heard this, convicted by their conscience, they went out one by one, beginning with the elders, until he himself was left alone, and the woman was standing in the midst.
Then Jesus straightened up and saw no one but the woman, and he said to her: "Where are your accusers? Has no one condemned you?"
She said to him: "No one, Lord!" And Jesus said to her: "Neither do I condemn you. Go, and from now on sin no more."
Again Jesus spoke to them and said: "I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness, but will have the light of life."
The Pharisees said to him: "You bear witness about yourself, and your testimony is not true."

Jesus answered and said to them: Even if I bear witness about myself, my witness is true, for I know where I have come from and where I am going; but you do not know where I came from or where I am going.
You judge according to the flesh, but I judge no one.
If I do judge, my judgment is true, for I am not alone; it is I and the Father who sent me.
For it is also written in your law that the witness of two men is true.
I am the one who bears witness about myself, and the Father who sent me bears witness about me.
The Jews said to him: Where is your Father? Jesus answered and said to them: You know neither me nor my Father. If you knew me, you would know my Father also.
He spoke these words by the treasury as he was teaching in the temple, and no one seized him, for his hour had not yet come.
Then Jesus said to them again: I am going away, and you will seek me and will not find me, and you will die in your sins; and where I am going, you cannot come.
The Jews said to one another: Will he perhaps kill himself? For he says, "Where I am going, you cannot come."
And Jesus said to them: You are from the earth, but I am from heaven; you are of this world, but I am not of this world.
I told you that you will die in your sins. If you do not believe me, that I am he, you will die in your sins.
They said to him: And who are you? Jesus said to them: First of all, that I am speaking to you:
I have many things to say about you and to judge, but the one who sent me is true, and what I have heard from him, that I speak in this world.
But they did not understand that he was telling them about his Father.
Then Jesus said to them: When you lift up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am he, and that I do nothing of myself, but as the Father taught me, so I speak.
And the one who sent me is with me; the Father has not left me alone, for I always do what is pleasing to him.
As he was saying this, many believed in him.
And Jesus said to those Jews who had believed in him: If you abide in my words, you are truly my disciples.
And you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free.
The Jews answered and said to him: We are the descendants of Abraham and have never been slaves to anyone. How is it that you say, "You will be set free"?
Jesus answered and said to them: Amen, amen, I say to you: everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin.
And the slave does not remain in the house forever, but the son remains forever.
If the Son sets you free, you will be truly free.
I know that you are descendants of Abraham, but you seek to kill me, because my word finds no place among you.
What I have seen with my Father, that I speak; and what you have seen with your father, that you do.
They answered and said to him, "Our father is Abraham." Jesus answered and said to them, "If you were children of Abraham, you would do the works of Abraham.
But now you seek to kill me, a man who tells you the truth, which I heard from God. Abraham did not do this.
But you do the work of your father." They said to him, "We were not born of fornication. We know one father: God."
Jesus said to them, "If God were your father, you would love me, for I came out from God and have come. For I have not come of myself; he sent me.
Why do you not understand my words? Because you cannot hear my words.

You are of your father the devil, and you want to do the desires of your father. For he was a murderer from the beginning, and he did not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he tells a lie, he speaks from his own heart, for he is a liar, and his father too is a liar.
But I tell you the truth, and you do not believe me.
Which of you convicts me of sin? If I tell you the truth, why do you not believe me?
Whoever is of God hears the words of God. You do not hear them for this reason: because you are not of God."
The Jews answered and said to him, "Did we not say rightly that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?"
Jesus answered and said to them, "I do not have a demon. Rather, I honor my Father, and you dishonor me.
But I do not seek my own glory. There is one who seeks it and judges.
Amen, amen, I say to you: if anyone keeps my word, he will never see death."
The Jews said to him, "Now we know that you are possessed by a demon. Abraham died, and the prophets too, and you say, 'If anyone keeps my word, he will never taste death.'
Are you greater than our father Abraham, who died? And the prophets died. Who do you make yourself out to be?"
Jesus answered and said to them, "If I glorify myself, my glory is nothing. It is my Father who glorifies me, of whom you say, 'He is our God.'
And you do not know him, but I know him. If I were to say that I do not know him, I would be a liar like you. But I know him, and I keep his word.
Your father Abraham rejoiced that he would see this day of mine. He saw it and was glad."
The Jews said to him, "You are not yet fifty years old, and you have seen Abraham?"
Jesus said to them, "Amen, amen, I say to you: before Abraham came to be, I am."
The Jews picked up stones to throw at him. But Jesus hid himself and went out of the temple. He passed through their midst and went away like this.
And as Jesus was walking along, he saw a man who had been blind from birth.
His disciples asked him, saying, "Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?"
Jesus said to them, "Neither this man sinned nor his parents. It happened so that the work of God might be revealed in him.
And I must do the work of the one who sent me while it is still day. Night is coming, when no one can work.
While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.
And when he had said this, he spat on the ground and made clay from the spittle, and he anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay
and said to him, "Go, wash in the pool of Siloam" (which is translated "Sent"). The man went and washed, and came back seeing.
Then the neighbours, and those who had seen him before, because he had been a beggar, were saying, "Is this not the one who used to sit and beg?"
Others were saying, "It is he." But some were saying, "No, but he is like him." But he kept saying, "I am he."
They asked him, "How were your eyes opened?"
He answered and said to them, "The man called Jesus made clay and anointed my eyes, and said to me, 'Go to the pool of Siloam and wash.' I went and washed, and I received my sight."
They said to him, "Where is he?" And he said to them, "I do not know."
It was the Sabbath when Jesus made the clay and opened his eyes.
They brought the man who had formerly been blind before the Pharisees.
The Pharisees also asked him again, "How did you receive your sight?" And he said to them, "He put clay on my eyes, and I washed, and now I see."
Some of the Pharisees were saying, "This man is not from God, because he does not keep the Sabbath." Others were saying, "How can a sinful man do such a sign?" And there was a dispute among them.
They said to the man who had formerly been blind, "What do you say about him, since he opened your eyes?" And he said to them, "He is a prophet."
The Jews did not believe about him that he had been blind and had received his sight, until they called the parents of the one who had received his sight.
They asked them and said, "Is this your son, of whom you say that he was born blind? How then does he now see?"
His parents answered and said, "We know that this is our son and that he was born blind.
But how he now sees, we do not know; or who opened his eyes, we do not know. Ask him; he is of age; let him speak for himself."
His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jews, for the Jews had agreed that if anyone confessed him as Christ, they would expel him from the synagogue.
That is why his parents said, "He is of age; ask him."
A second time they called the man who had formerly been blind, and said to him, "Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner."
But he answered and said, "Whether he is a sinner, I do not know. But this one thing I know: that I was blind and now I see."
Then they said to him, "What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?"
He answered and said to them, "I told you already, and you did not listen. Why do you want to hear it again? Or do you also want to become his disciples?"
But they reviled him and said, "You are his disciple, but we are disciples of Moses.
We know that God spoke to Moses, but as for this man, we do not know where he is from."
The man answered and said to them: "This is a marvel, that you do not know where he is from, and yet he opened my eyes.
This I know: God does not listen to a sinner. But if anyone is a worshipper of God and does God's will, God listens to him.
Since the beginning of the world it has never been heard that anyone opened the eyes of a man born blind.
If this man were not from God, he could not do anything."
They answered and said to him: "You were born entirely in sins, and you are teaching us?" And they drove him out.
Jesus heard that they had driven him out. He found him and said to him: "Do you believe in the Son of God?"
He answered and said: "Who is he, Lord, so that I may believe in him?"
Jesus said to him: "You have seen him, and the one who is speaking with you is he."
And he said to him: "I believe, Lord," and he worshipped him.
And Jesus said: "I have come into this world for judgment, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind."
Some of the Pharisees who were with him heard this and said: "Surely we are not blind too?"
Jesus said to them: "If you were blind, you would have no sin. But now you say, 'We see,' and so your sins remain.
Amen, amen, I say to you: whoever does not enter the sheepfold by the door but climbs in some other way is a thief and a robber.
But the one who enters by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
The doorkeeper opens to him, and the sheep listen to his voice, and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
And when he has led out all his own, he walks ahead of them, and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice.
But they will not follow a stranger; they flee from him, because they do not know the stranger's voice."
Jesus told them this parable, but they did not understand what he was saying to them.
So Jesus said to them again: "Amen, amen, I say to you: I am the door of the sheep.
All who came before me were thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them.
I am the door. If anyone enters through me, he will be saved; he will go in and go out and find pasture.
The thief comes only to steal and kill and destroy. But I have come so that they may have life, and have it more abundantly.
I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
But the hired man, who is not the shepherd and does not own the sheep, sees the wolf coming, leaves the sheep and runs away, and the wolf snatches them and scatters them.
For he is a hired man and does not care at all about the sheep.
I am the good shepherd, and I know my own, and my own know me.
As the Father knows me, I also know the Father, and I lay down my life for the sheep.
And I have other sheep, which are not of this fold; I must bring them too, and they will hear my voice, and there will be one flock and one shepherd.
For this reason the Father loves me, because I lay down my life, so that I may take it up again.
No one takes it from me, but I lay it down of my own accord. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it up again. This commandment I have received from my Father.
And there was again a division among the Jews because of these words.
And many of them were saying: "He has a demon and is raving. Why do you listen to him?"
And others were saying: "These are not the words of one who has a demon. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?"
And at that time the Feast of Dedication took place in Jerusalem; it was winter.
And Jesus was walking in the temple, in the portico of Solomon.
The Jews gathered around him and said to him: "How long will you keep our souls in suspense? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly."
Jesus answered and said: "I told you, and you do not believe. The works that I do in the name of my Father, these bear witness about me.
And you do not believe me, because you are not of my sheep, as I told you.
My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.
And I will give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hands.
My Father, who has given them to me, is greater than all, and no one is able to snatch them out of the hands of my Father.
I and my Father are one."
The Jews again took up stones to stone him.
Jesus answered and said to them: "I have shown you many good works from my Father; for which of those works are you stoning me?"
The Jews answered and said to him: "We are not stoning you for a good work, but for blasphemy, and because you, being a man, have made yourself God."
Jesus answered and said to them: "Is it not written in the law: 'I said, you are gods'?
If he called them gods, to whom the word of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken,
do you say of him whom the Father sanctified and sent into the world, 'He blasphemes,' because I said, 'I am the Son of God'?
If I do not do the works of my Father, do not believe me.
But if I do them, even though you do not believe me, believe the works, so that you may understand and know that the Father is in me, and I am in the Father."
They sought again to seize him, and he went out from their hands.
And he went away across the Jordan, to the place where John had first baptized, and he stayed there.
And many came to him and said: "John did no sign; but everything that John said about this man was true."
And many believed in him there.
A certain man was sick, Lazarus of Bethany, from the village of Mary and Martha, her sister.
This was the Mary who anointed the Lord with ointment and wiped his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was sick.
His sisters sent to Jesus and said to him: "Lord, behold, the one whom you love is sick."
But when Jesus heard it, he said: "This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it."
Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus.
When he heard that he was sick, he then stayed on two more days in the place where he was.
Then, after this, he said to his disciples: "Come, let us go again into Judea."
The disciples said to him: "Teacher, just now the Jews were seeking to stone you, and are you going there again?"
Jesus said to him: "Are there not twelve hours in the day? If anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world.
And if anyone walks in the night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him."
He said this, and after this he said to them: "Lazarus, my friend, has fallen asleep, but I will go and awaken him."
The disciples said to him: "Lord, if he has fallen asleep, he will recover."
But Jesus had spoken of his death, and they thought that he spoke of resting in sleep.
Then Jesus said to them plainly: "Lazarus has died.
And I am glad for your sakes, so that you may believe in me, that I was not there. But come, let us go to him."
Then Thomas, who was called Didymus (the Twin), said to his fellow disciples: "Come, let us go, so that we too may die with him."
And when Jesus came to Bethany, he found that he had already been four days in the tomb.
Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, only about fifteen stadia away.
And many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary to comfort them concerning their brother.
But when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went to meet him, while Mary sat in the house.
Martha said to Jesus: "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died,
But even now I know that whatever you ask of God, God will give you.
Jesus said to her, "Your brother will rise again."
Martha said to him, "I know that he will rise again in the resurrection on the last day."
Jesus said to her, "I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, even if he dies, will live."
And everyone who is alive and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?"
Martha said to him, "Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who is coming into the world."
And when she had said this, she went and secretly called Mary, her sister, and said to her, "The Teacher has come and is calling you."
And when she heard this, she got up quickly and went to him.
For Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was still at the place where Martha had met him.
But the Jews who were with her in the house and were consoling them, when they saw that Mary got up quickly and went out, followed her, thinking that she was going to the tomb to weep there.
And when Mary came to where Jesus was and saw him, she fell at his feet and said to him, "Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died."
And when Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her also weeping, he was deeply troubled in spirit, as if with anger,
and he said to them, "Where have you laid him?" They said to him, "Come and see!"
And Jesus too shed tears.
So the Jews said, "See how much he loved him!"
But some of them said, "Could not this man, who opened the eyes of the blind man, have done something so that this man also would not have died?"
Then Jesus, again as if angered within himself, came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone lay upon it.
Jesus said to them, "Take away that stone!" Martha, the sister of the dead man, said to him, "Lord, by now he stinks, for it is the fourth day."
Jesus said to her, "Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?"
So they took away the stone from where the dead man lay. And Jesus lifted up his eyes to heaven and said, "Father, I thank you that you have heard me,
and I know that you always hear me, but I said this for the sake of the people standing around me, so that they may believe that you sent me."
And when he had said this, he cried out with a loud voice, "Lazarus, come out!"
And the dead man came out, his hands and feet bound with wrappings, and his face was covered with a cloth. Jesus said to them, "Unbind him and let him go!"
So many of the Jews who had come to Mary and Martha saw what Jesus had done and believed in him.
But some of them went and told the Pharisees what Jesus had done.
Then the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered a council and said, "What are we to do? For this man is performing many signs.
If we let him go on like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away from us both our place and our nation."
One of them, Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them, "You know nothing at all,
nor have you considered that it is better for us that one man should die for the people, and not that the whole nation should perish."
He did not say this of his own accord. Being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus was going to die for the nation,
and not for the nation only, but also to gather into one the scattered children of God.
From that day on the Jews plotted together to kill him.
So Jesus no longer walked openly among the Jews. Instead he went away from there to the country near the wilderness, to a town called Ephraim, and he stayed there with his disciples.
Now the Passover of the Jews was near, and many went up from the countryside to Jerusalem before the Passover to purify themselves.
The Jews were looking for Jesus, and as they stood in the temple they said to one another, "What do you think? Will he not come to the feast?"
For the chief priests and the Pharisees had given an order that if anyone knew where he was, he should report it to them, so that they might arrest him.
Six days before his Passion, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, who had died and whom he had raised from the dead.
They prepared a supper for him there. Martha served him, and Lazarus was one of those reclining at table with him.
Then Mary took a pound of ointment of pure, very costly nard and anointed Jesus' feet, and wiped his feet with her hair. The whole house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment.
One of his disciples, Judas Iscariot, son of Simon, who was going to betray him, said,
"Why was this ointment not sold for three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor?"
He said this not because he cared in his heart for the poor, but because he was a thief; he had the money box and carried what was put into it.
Jesus said, "Leave her alone. She has kept this for the day of my burial.
For the poor are always with you, but I am not always with you."
Then the whole crowd of the Jews learned that Jesus was there, and they came not only because of Jesus but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.
So the chief priests plotted to kill Lazarus as well,
because on his account many of the Jews were going over and believing in Jesus.
The next day the great crowd that had come to the feast, having heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,
took branches of palm trees and went out to meet him, crying out and saying, "Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!"
And Jesus found a donkey and sat on it, as it is written:
"Do not be afraid, daughter of Zion! Behold, your king is coming to you, and he is seated on the colt of a donkey."
His disciples did not understand this at first, but when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that this had been written about him, and that they had done these things to him.
And the crowd that had been with him when he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead bore witness to him.
This is also why the crowd went out to meet him: they had heard that Jesus had done this sign.
But the Pharisees said to one another, "Do you see that you are gaining nothing? Behold, the whole world has gone after him."
There were also some Gentiles among those who had come up to worship at the feast.
These came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and said to him, "Lord, we wish to see Jesus."
Philip went and told Andrew; and Andrew and Philip came and told Jesus.
And Jesus answered and said to them, "The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
Amen, amen, I tell you: unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
Whoever loves his life will lose it; and whoever hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life.
If anyone serves me, let him follow me; and where I am, there my servant will be also. And if anyone serves me, my Father will honor him.
Now my soul is troubled, and what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour? But for this purpose I came to this hour.
Father, glorify your Son." A voice came to him from heaven: "I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again."
The crowd that stood there and heard it said, "It was thunder"; but others said, "An angel spoke to him."
Jesus answered and said to them, "This voice did not come for my sake, but for yours.
Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be cast out.
And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself."
He said this to show by what kind of death he was going to die.
The crowd answered him and said, "We have heard from the Law that the Christ remains forever. How then can you say, 'The Son of Man must be lifted up'? Who is this Son of Man?"

Jesus said to them, "The light is with you for a little while longer. Walk while you still have the light, so that darkness may not overtake you; for whoever walks in darkness does not know where he is going.
While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may become sons of light." Jesus said these things, and he went away and hid himself from them.
Though he had done so many signs before them, they did not believe in him,
so that the word of the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled, which he says: "Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?"
For this reason they could not believe, because Isaiah also said again:
"He has blinded their eyes, so that they may not see with their eyes, and hardened their hearts, so that they may not understand with their hearts and turn, and I would heal them."
Isaiah said this when he saw his glory and spoke about him.
Yet even among the rulers many believed in him, but because of the Pharisees they did not confess it, so that they would not be put out of the synagogue,
for they loved the glory of men more than the glory of God.
Then Jesus cried out and said: "Whoever believes in me does not believe in me, but in the one who sent me.
And whoever has seen me has seen the one who sent me.
I, the light, have been sent into the world, so that everyone who believes in me may not remain in darkness.
And if anyone hears my words and does not believe them, I do not judge him, for I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world.
But whoever despises me and does not receive my words has his own judge: the word that I have spoken, that will judge him on the last day.
For I have spoken nothing of my own accord; but the one who sent me, the Father, he gave me a commandment about what I should say and what I should speak.
And I know that his commandment is eternal life. And what I speak, I speak just as the Father has commanded me."

Now before the feast of the Passover, Jesus knew that his hour had come to depart out of this world and go to the Father; for he had loved his own who were in this world, and he loved them to the end.
And while the supper was taking place, and the devil had already entered into the heart of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, so that he would betray him,
Jesus, knowing that the Father had given everything into his hands, and that he had come from God and was going to God,
rose from the supper, laid aside his garment, took a towel, and girded himself with it.
And he took water and poured it into the basin, and began to wash the feet of his disciples and to wipe them with the towel with which he was girded.
And he came to Simon Peter. Peter said to him: "Lord, are you going to wash my feet?"
Jesus answered and said to him: "What I am doing you do not know now, but you will understand afterwards."
Peter said to him: "You shall never wash my feet." Jesus said to him: "If I do not wash your feet, you have no share with me."
Simon Peter said to him: "Lord, not only my feet, but also my hands and my head."
Jesus said to him: "One who has bathed has no need except to wash only his feet, for he is wholly clean; and you are clean, but not all of you."
For Jesus knew who was to betray him. That is why he said: "Not all of you are clean."
And when he had washed their feet, he took his garment and reclined at table, and then he said to them: "Do you know what I have done to you?
You call me 'Teacher' and 'Lord', and you say well, for so I am.
If I, the Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet.
For I have given you an example, so that just as I have done to you, you also should do.
Amen, amen, I say to you: a servant is not greater than his lord, nor is an apostle greater than the one who sent him.
If you know these things, you are blessed if you do them.
I do not speak of all of you, for I know those whom I have chosen; but it is so that the Scriptures may be fulfilled: “He who ate bread with me has lifted up his heel against me.”
From now on I tell you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe that I am he.
Amen, I say to you: whoever receives the one I send receives me; and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me.
When Jesus had said this, he was troubled in spirit, and he testified and said: “Amen, amen, I say to you that one of you will betray me.”
So the disciples looked at one another and did not know of whom he was speaking.
And one of his disciples, the one whom Jesus loved, was reclining at Jesus' bosom.
Simon Peter beckoned to him to ask who it was of whom he was speaking.
So he leaned back on Jesus' breast and said to him: “Lord, who is it?”
Jesus answered and said: “It is the one to whom I give the bread after I have dipped it.” And he dipped the bread and gave it to Judas, son of Simon, the Iscariot.
And after Judas received the bread, the devil entered into him. And Jesus said to him: “What you intend to do, do quickly!”
But none of those reclining at table with Jesus understood why he said this to him.
For some thought that, since Judas had the money bag, Jesus was telling him: “Buy what we need for this feast,” or that he should give something to the poor.
So he took the bread and went out at once. And it was night.
And when Judas had gone out, Jesus said: “Now the Son of Man has been glorified, and God has been glorified in him.
If God has been glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself, and will glorify him at once.
Children, I am with you a little while longer. You will seek me, and just as I said to the Jews, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come,’ so now I say to you.
A new commandment I give you, that you love one another; just as I have loved you, you also should love one another.
By this all will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.”
Simon Peter said to him: “Lord, where are you going?” Jesus said to him: “Where I am going, you cannot follow me now, but afterward you will follow me.”
Peter said to him: “Lord, why can I not follow you? Now I will lay down my life for you.”
Jesus answered and said to him: “Will you lay down your life for me? Amen, amen, I say to you: the cock will not crow until you have denied me three times.”
“Do not let your hearts be troubled; believe in God, and believe in me.”
In my Father's house there are many dwelling places. If it were not so, I would have told you that I am going to prepare a place for you.
And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again and take you to myself, so that where I am, there you also may be.
And where I am going, you know, and you know the way as well.
Thomas said to him: "Lord, we do not know where you are going, so how can we know the way?"
Jesus said to him: "I am the way, and I am the truth and the life; no one comes to the Father except through me."
If you had known me, you would have known my Father also. From now on you know him, and you have seen him.
Philip said to him: "Lord, show us your Father, and that is enough for us."
Jesus said to him: "I have been with you all this time, and you do not know me, Philip? Whoever has seen me has seen my Father. So how can you say to me, 'Show us your Father'?"
Do you not believe that I am with the Father and my Father is with me? The words that I speak to you I do not speak on my own, but my Father, who is with me, he is the one who does the work.
Do you believe that I am with the Father and my Father is with me? If not, then believe me because of these works.
Amen, amen, I tell you: whoever believes in me will also do the work that I do, and he will do even greater things than this, because I am going to the Father.
And whatever you ask in my name, I will do it, so that the Father may be glorified with the Son.
If you love me, keep my commandments!
And I will ask my Father, and he will send you another Comforter, to remain with you forever:
the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it does not see him and does not know him, because he is with you and will be with you.
I will not leave you orphans; I will come to you.
In a little while this world will no longer see me, but you will see me, because I am alive, and you too will live.
On that day you will know that I am with my Father, and you are with me, and I am among you.
Whoever has my commandments and keeps them is the one who loves me. And whoever loves me will be loved by my Father, and I too will love him and reveal myself to him.
Judas (not Iscariot) said to him: "Lord, why is it that you will reveal yourself to us and not to the world?"
Jesus answered and said to him: "If anyone loves me, he will keep my words, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and remain with him.
But whoever does not love me does not keep my words. And the words that you hear are not mine, but belong to my Father who sent me.
I have told you these things because I was with you.
But the Comforter, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything and will remind you of everything I have told you.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not let them be afraid.
You heard that I said to you, 'I am going away, and I will come to you.' If you loved me, you would rejoice that I am going to my Father, for my Father is greater than I.
And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe.
I will no longer say much with you, for the ruler of this world is coming, and he will find nothing in me.
But so that the world may know that I love the Father, and that as the Father commanded me, so I do — rise, let us go from here!
I am the true vine, and my Father is the vinedresser.
Every branch that is in me and does not bear fruit, he takes away; and every one that bears fruit, he cleanses, so that it may bring forth more fruit.
But you are already clean through the word that I have spoken to you.
Abide in me, and I in you. Just as the branch cannot bring forth fruit by itself unless it remains on the vine, so neither can you unless you abide in me.
I am the vine, and you are the branches. Whoever abides in me, and I in him, he will bear much fruit, for without me you can do nothing, not even one thing.
If anyone does not abide in me, he is thrown out like a branch and withers, and they gather it and throw it into the fire, and it is burned.
If you abide in me, and my words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.
By this my Father is glorified, that you bring forth much fruit and become my disciples.
As the Father has loved me, so I have loved you; abide in my love!
If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love, just as I have kept my Father's commandments and remain in his love.
I have said this to you so that my joy may remain in you, and that your joy may be complete.
For this is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.
No one has greater love than this, that he lay down his life for his friends.
You are my friends if you do what I command you.
I no longer call you servants, for the servant does not know what his master is doing. But I have called you friends, for everything that I heard from my Father I have made known to you.

You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you, so that you may go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit may remain in fullness, so that whatever you ask of my Father in my name, he may give it to you.
This I command you, that you love one another.
If the world hates you, know that it hated me first.
If you were of the world, the world would love its own. Because you are not of the world, but I chose you out of the world, for this reason the world hates you.
Remember the word that I said to you: 'A servant is not greater than his master.' If they persecuted me, they will persecute you too; if they kept my words, they will keep yours too.
But they will do all this to you for my name's sake, because they do not know the one who sent me.
If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have had sin; but now they have no excuse for their sins.
Whoever hates me hates my Father also.
If I had not done among them the works that no one else did, they would not have had sin. But now they have seen me, and they have hated both me and my Father,
But this is so that the word might be fulfilled which is written in their law: "They hated me without cause."
But when the Comforter comes, whom I will send to you from my Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, he will bear witness about me.
And you also are witnesses, because you have been with me from the beginning.
I have told you these things so that you may not stumble.
They will put you out of the synagogue. Indeed, the hour is coming when everyone who kills you will think that he has offered a sacrifice to God.
And they will do this to you because they have not known the Father who sent me, nor me.
But I have told you this so that, when that hour comes, you may remember these things, because I told you. I did not tell you this from the beginning, because I was with you.
But now I am going to the one who sent me, and none of you asks me, "Where are you going?"
But because I have told you this, sorrow has filled your hearts.
But I tell you the truth: it is better for you that I go away. If I do not go away, the Comforter will not come to you; if I go away, I will send him to you.
And he will come and convict the world concerning sin and concerning righteousness and concerning judgement:
concerning sin, in this way: because they did not believe in me;
and concerning righteousness, because I am going to my Father, and you will no longer see me;
and concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
I still have much to say to you, but you cannot bear it now.
But when the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all truth, for he will not speak on his own, but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will tell you what is to come.
He will glorify me, for he will receive from me and tell it to you.
Everything that the Father has is mine; and that is why I told you that he will take from what is mine and tell it to you.
A little while longer, and you will no longer see me; and again a little while, and you will see me, because I am going to my Father.

So his disciples said to one another, "What is this that he is saying to us: 'A little while longer, and you will no longer see me'; and 'Again a little while, and you will see me'; and 'Because I am going to my Father'?"
So they were saying, "What is this 'little while'? We do not know what he is talking about."

Jesus understood that they wanted to ask him, and he said to them, "Are you asking one another about this, because I said, 'A little while longer, and you will no longer see me'; and 'Again a little while, and you will see me'?

Amen, amen, I say to you: you will weep and [?] (the text has "you will think", probably an error for "you will lament"), but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy.

When a woman gives birth she is in sorrow, because her hour has come. But when she has borne the child, she no longer remembers the anguish because of the joy that a human being has been born into the world.
And you now have anguish. But I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy away from you.
And on that day you will ask me nothing. Amen, amen, I say to you: whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give it to you.
Until now you have asked for nothing in my name. Ask and you will receive, so that your joy may be complete.
I have told you this in parables. But the hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in parables, but will tell you plainly about my Father.
On that day you will ask in my name, and I do not tell you that I will ask my Father on your behalf.
For my Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came forth from God.
I came forth from the Father and came into the world, and again I leave the world and go to the Father.
His disciples said to him: "Look, now you are speaking plainly, and you are not speaking in any parable."
"And now we know that you know all things and have no need for anyone to question you. Because of this we believe that you came forth from God."
Jesus answered and said to them: "Do you now believe?"
Look, the hour is coming and has arrived when you will be scattered, each one to his own place, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, for my Father is with me.
I have told you these things so that you may have peace in me. In this world you have tribulation, but do not be afraid, for I have overcome the world.
Jesus said these things, and he lifted up his eyes to heaven and said: "Father, my hour has come. Glorify your Son, so that your Son may also glorify you.
Just as you gave him authority over all flesh, so that to all whom you have given him he may give eternal life.
And this is eternal life: that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you sent.
I glorified you on earth; I completed the work that you gave me to do.
And now, Father, glorify me with yourself, with the glory that I had in your presence before the creation of the world.
I have revealed your name to the people whom you gave me out of this world. They were yours, and you gave them to me, and they have kept your word.
And now they have come to know that everything you have given me is from you.
For the words that you gave me I have given to them, and they received them and knew truly that I came forth from you, and they believed that you sent me.
I am asking on their behalf. I am not asking on behalf of the world, but on behalf of those whom you have given me, for they are yours.
And all that is mine is yours, and what is yours is mine, and I am glorified among them.
And I am no longer in this world, but these are in the world, and I am coming to you. Holy Father, keep these whom you have given me in your name, so that they may be one, just as we are.
When I was with them in the world, I kept them in your name. Those whom you gave me I guarded, and none of them was lost except the son of perdition, so that the scripture might be fulfilled.
But now I am coming to you, and I say these things in the world so that they may have my joy in full.
I have given them your words, and the world has hated them, because they are not of this world, just as I am not of this world.
I do not ask that you take them out of the world, but that you keep them from evil.
They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.
Sanctify them in truth, for your word is truth.
Just as you sent me into the world, I also send them into the world.
And for their sake I sanctify myself, so that they too may be holy in truth.
And I do not ask for these alone, but for all who will believe in me through their word,
so that all may be one, as you, Father, are in me and I in you, so that they too may be one in us, so that the world may believe that you sent me.
