And the glory that you gave me I have given to them, so that they may be one, as we are one.
I in them and you with me, so that they may be in perfect unity, and so that the world may know that you sent me and loved them as you loved me.
Father, I desire that those whom you have given me may be with me where I am, so that they may see my glory, which you gave me, for you loved me before the creation of the world.
Righteous Father, the world did not know you, but I knew you, and these too knew that you sent me.
And I made your name known to them, and I will make it known, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them, and I with them.
When Jesus had said this, he went out with his disciples across the Valley of the Cedars, where there was a garden, which he and his disciples entered.
Judas, who betrayed him, also knew the place, because Jesus had often gone there with his disciples.
So Judas took the band of soldiers and servants from the chief priests and the Pharisees, and came there with candles, lamps and weapons.
But Jesus, knowing everything that was coming upon him, went out and said to them, "Whom are you seeking?"
They answered and said to him, "Jesus of Nazareth." Jesus said to them, "I am he." Judas, who betrayed him, was also standing with them.
And when he said to them, "I am he," they drew back and fell to the ground.
Then he asked them again, "Whom are you seeking?" And they said to him, "Jesus of Nazareth."
Jesus said to them, "I told you that I am he. If you are seeking me, let these go away,"
so that the word he had spoken might be fulfilled: "Of those whom you gave me, I have not lost even one."
Then Simon Peter, who had a sword, drew it and struck the high priest's servant and cut off his right ear. The servant's name was Malchus.
Jesus said to Peter, "Put the sword into its sheath! The cup that the Father has given me, shall I not drink it?"
Then the band of soldiers, the commander and the servants of the Jews seized Jesus and bound him.
And they led him first to Annas, for he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
It was this Caiaphas who had advised the Jews that it was better for one man to die for the people.
Simon Peter and the other disciple followed Jesus. That other disciple was known to the high priest, and he went with Jesus into the high priest's courtyard.
But Peter stood outside by the door. So the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the woman who kept the door, and brought Peter in.
The servant girl who kept the door said to Peter, "Surely you are not also one of this man's disciples?" But Peter said, "I am not."
The slaves and servants of the high priests were standing there; they had lit a charcoal fire, because it was cold, and were warming themselves. Peter also was standing with them and warming himself.
Then the high priest asked Jesus about his disciples and about his teaching.
Jesus answered and said to him: "I have spoken openly to the world. I always taught in the synagogue and in the temple, where all the Jews gather, and I said nothing in secret.
Why do you ask me? Ask those who heard what I taught them. Look, these people know what I said to them."
When Jesus had said this, one of the attendants standing there struck Jesus on the cheek and said: "Is this how you answer the high priest?"
Jesus said to him: "If I have spoken wrongly, testify about the wrong; but if rightly, why do you strike me?"
And Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas the high priest.
Now Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. Those standing there said to him: "Surely you are not also one of his disciples?" But he denied it and said: "I am not."
One of the high priest's servants, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, said to him: "Did I not see you in the garden with him?"
And Peter denied it again, and at once the cock crowed.
Then they brought Jesus from Caiaphas to the praetorium. It was early morning. They themselves did not go into the praetorium, so that they would not be defiled, but could eat the Passover.
Pilate came out to them and said to them: "What accusation do you bring against this man?"
They answered and said to him: "If he were not an evildoer, we would not have handed him over to you."
Pilate said to them: "Take him yourselves and judge him according to your law!" The Jews said to him: "It is not lawful for us to put anyone to death."
This was so that the word of Jesus would be fulfilled, which he had spoken to show by what death he was going to die.
So Pilate went back into the praetorium, called Jesus, and said to him: "Are you the king of the Jews?"
Jesus said to him: "Do you say this of your own accord, or did others tell you about me?"
Pilate answered and said to him: "Am I a Jew? Your own people and the high priests have handed you over to me. What have you done?"

Jesus answered and said to him: "My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, my servants would be fighting for me, so that I would not be handed over to the Jews. But now my kingdom is not from here."

Pilate said to him: "So you are a king?" Jesus said to him: "You say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I was sent into the world: to bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth hears my voice."
Pilate said to him: "What is truth?" When he had said this, he went out again and said to the Jews: "I find no fault at all in him.
But you have a custom that I release one man to you at this feast. Do you want me to release to you the king of the Jews?"
Then they all cried out again and said: "Not him, but Barabbas!" Now this Barabbas was a robber.
Then Pilate took Jesus and had him scourged.
And the soldiers wove a crown of thorns, put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple robe.
They kept coming up to him and saying to him: "Hail, king of the Jews!" And they struck him on the cheek.
Then Pilate went out again and said to them: "Look, I am bringing him out to you, so that you may know that I have found no fault at all in him."
Jesus came out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe. And Pilate said to them: "Here is the man!"
When the chief priests and the servants saw him, they cried out and said: "Crucify, crucify him!" Pilate said to them: "Take him yourselves and crucify him, for I find no fault in him."
The Jews answered and said to him: "We have a law, and by our law he deserves death, because he made himself the Son of God."
When Pilate heard this word, he was even more afraid.
He went back into the praetorium and said to Jesus: "Where are you from?" But Jesus gave him no answer.
Pilate said to him: "Will you say nothing to me? Do you not know that I have authority to crucify you and authority to release you?"
Jesus said to him: "You would have no authority over me at all if it had not been given to you from above. Therefore the one who handed me over to you has the greater sin."
From then on Pilate wanted to release him, but the Jews cried out and said: "If you release him, you are no friend of Caesar, for everyone who calls himself a king speaks against Caesar."
When Pilate heard this word, he brought Jesus out and sat down on the judgment seat, in the place called the Pavement, and in Hebrew Gabbatha.
It was the day of Preparation for the Passover, and it was about the sixth hour. Pilate said to the Jews: "Here is your king!"
But they cried out and said: "Take him away, take him away and crucify him!" Pilate said to them: "Shall I crucify your king?" The chief priests answered and said: "We have no king but Caesar."
Then he handed him over to them to be crucified, and they led Jesus away.
He carried his own cross and went out to the place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
There they crucified him, and with him two others, one on each side, with Jesus in the middle.
Pilate wrote a notice on a board and put it on the cross. It said: "Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews."
Many of the Jews read this notice, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city. It was written in Hebrew, in Latin and in Greek.
So the chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate: "Do not write 'The King of the Jews', but that he said, 'I am the King of the Jews.'"
Pilate said to them: "What I have written, I have written."
The soldiers who crucified Jesus took his garments and divided them into four parts, one part for each soldier. But the tunic was seamless, woven in one piece from the top all the way down,

so they said to one another: "Let us not tear it, but let us cast lots for it to see whose it will be." This happened so that the scripture would be fulfilled: "They divided my garments among themselves, and for my tunic they cast lots." So the soldiers did these things.
Standing by the cross of Jesus were his mother, his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
When Jesus saw his mother, and the disciple whom he loved standing near her, he said to his mother: "Woman, here is your son!"
Then he said to the disciple: "Here is your mother!" And from that time on the disciple took her into his own home.
After this, Jesus saw that everything had been accomplished, and so that the scripture might be fulfilled, he said: "I am thirsty."
A vessel full of vinegar stood there. They filled a sponge with the vinegar, together with hyssop, put it on a reed, and held it to his mouth.
When Jesus had received the vinegar, he said: "This scripture too has been fulfilled." He bowed his head and gave up his spirit.

Since it was Friday, the Jews did not want his body to remain on the cross until the Sabbath, because the day of that Sabbath was a great day. So they asked Pilate to have their legs broken and to have them taken down.
The soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man, and likewise of the other, who had been crucified with him.
But when they came to Jesus and saw that he had already died, they did not break his legs.
Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a lance, and at once blood and water came out.
The one who saw it has borne witness, and his testimony is true. He knows that he speaks the truth, so that you also may believe.
This happened so that the scripture might be fulfilled: "His bone shall not be broken."
And another scripture says: "They shall look on the one whom they pierced."

After this, Joseph, who was from Arimathea, asked Pilate if he could take away the body of Jesus. Joseph was a disciple of Jesus, but secretly, because he was afraid of the Jews. Pilate gave him permission, so he came and took away his body.
Nicodemus also came, the one who had first come to Jesus by night. He brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds.
They took the body of Jesus and wrapped it in linen cloths with the spices, as is the burial custom of the Jews.
In the place where he was crucified there was a garden, and in the garden there was a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid.
Because it was the Jews' Friday, they laid the body of Jesus there, since the tomb was nearby.
On the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene came to the tomb at dawn, while it was still dark, and saw that the stone had been taken away from the entrance of the tomb.
She ran and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple, the one whom Jesus loved, and said to them: "They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and I do not know where they have laid him."
Peter and the other disciple went out and were going to the tomb.
The two of them were running together, but the other disciple ran ahead, faster than Peter, and reached the tomb first.
He looked down into the tomb and saw the linen cloths lying there by themselves, but he did not go in.
Then Simon Peter also came after him and went into the tomb. He saw the linen cloths lying there,
and the face cloth that had been on his head. It was not lying with the linen cloths but was folded up by itself in one place.
Then the other disciple, who had reached the tomb before Peter, also went in. And they saw it and believed.
For they did not yet understand the scripture, that he had to rise from the dead.
Then the disciples went back again to their own homes.
But Mary stood outside by the tomb, weeping. As she wept, she looked down into the tomb.
And she saw two angels clothed in white, sitting where the body of the Lord Jesus had lain, one at the head and one at the feet.
And the angels said to her, "Woman, why are you weeping?" And she said to them, "They have taken my Lord from the tomb, and I do not know where they have laid him."
When she had said this, she turned around and saw Jesus standing there, and she did not know that it was Jesus.

Jesus said to her, "Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you looking for?" She thought that he was the gardener, and she said to him, "Sir, if you have taken him away, tell me where you have laid him, and I will take him away."
Jesus said to her, "Mary!" She turned around and said to him in Hebrew, "Rabbouni!" (which means Teacher), and she ran to meet him.
Jesus said to her, "Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father. Go to my brothers and tell them: I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God."
Mary Magdalene came to tell his disciples that she had seen the Lord and that he had said this to her.

And when evening came on that day, the first day of the week, and the doors were shut where the disciples were gathered for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood among them and said to them, "Peace be with you!"
And when he had said this, he showed them his hands and his side. And the disciples rejoiced when they saw the Lord.
Jesus said to them again, "Peace be with you! As the Father has sent me, so I also send you."
And when he had said this, he breathed on them and said, "Receive the Holy Spirit!
If you forgive anyone's sins, they are forgiven them; and if you retain anyone's, they are retained."
But Thomas, one of the Twelve, who was called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.

The other disciples told him, "We have seen the Lord." But he said to them, "Unless I see the mark of the nails in his hands, and put my fingers into the place of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will never believe."
And after eight days his disciples were again inside, and Thomas was with them. And Jesus came in through the closed doors and stood among them and said to them, "Peace be with you!"
Then he said to Thomas, "Bring your fingers here and see my hands, and bring your hand, and do not be unbelieving, but believe."
Thomas answered and said to him, "My Lord and my God!"
Jesus said to him, "You have seen me, and you believe. Blessed are those who have not seen me and have believed in me."
Jesus also did many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book.
But these have been written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and so that you may believe and have life in his name.
After this Jesus showed himself again to his disciples by the Sea of Tiberias. And he showed himself in this way:
Simon Peter was there together with Thomas, who was called Didymus, and Nathanael, who was from Cana of Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two others of the disciples.
Simon Peter said to them, "I am going fishing." They said to him, "We will come with you too." They went out and got into the boat, and that night they caught nothing.
And as day was breaking, Jesus stood on the shore, and the disciples did not know that it was the Lord.
Jesus said to them, "Children, do you have anything to eat?" They answered him, "No."
And he said to them, "Cast that net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some." So they cast the net, and they could no longer haul it in because of the great number of fish.
The disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, "It is the Lord." When Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he put on his garment, for he was naked, and threw himself into the sea.
But the other disciples came in the boat, for they were not far from land, only about two hundred cubits off, dragging the net full of fish.
And when they got out onto the land, they saw a charcoal fire laid there, with fish on it, and bread.
Jesus said to them, "Bring some of the fish that you have caught."
Simon Peter also went up and hauled the net ashore, full of large fish, one hundred and fifty-three of them. There were so many, and yet the net was not torn.
Jesus said to them, "Come and have a meal!" And none of the disciples dared to ask him, "Who are you?" They all knew that it was the Lord.
Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and the fish likewise.
This was the third time that Jesus appeared to his disciples after he had risen from the dead.

And when they had eaten, Jesus said to Simon Peter, "Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me more than these?" Peter said to him, "Yes, Lord, you know that I love you." Jesus said to him, "Feed my lambs!"
He said to them again, a second time, "Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?" Peter said to him, "Yes, Lord, you know that I love you." Jesus said to him, "Shepherd my sheep!"

Again Jesus said to him a third time, "Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?" Peter was grieved because he said to him a third time, "Do you love me?" And he said to him, "Lord, you know all things and you understand all things; you know that I love you." Jesus said to him, "Shepherd my sheep!"

"Amen, amen, I say to you: when you were young, you girded yourself and walked wherever you wished. But when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will gird you and lead you where you do not want to go."
He said this to indicate by what death he would glorify God. And when he had said this, he said to him, "Follow me!"
Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following, the one who at the supper had leaned on his breast and said to him, "Lord, who is it that will betray you?"
When Peter saw him, he said to Jesus, "Lord, and what about this man?"
Jesus said to him, "If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me!"
And this saying went out among the brothers, that that disciple would not die. Yet Jesus did not say to him that he would not die, but, "If I want him to remain until my coming, what is that to you?"
This is the disciple who bears witness to these things and who wrote these things, and you know that his testimony is true.
And there are also many other things that Jesus did; if they were written down one by one, I do not think that this world could contain the books that would be written.
